title: ICE Detains 30+ Workers in Identity-Fraud Raid at Birmingham, Alabama Manufacturing Plant
detail: On June 30, 2026, ICE Homeland Security Investigations agents raided Scholar Craft, a manufacturing plant in Birmingham, Alabama, detaining more than 30 workers found to be in the country without legal status. The operation focused on identity fraud and illegal employment practices, including the alleged use of fake identification documents and stolen Social Security numbers to obtain employment — a pattern consistent with other 2026 worksite raids such as 'Operation Ghost Story' in Abbeville, South Carolina. The raid was part of an escalating wave of ICE worksite enforcement operations following the May 2026 deployment of roughly 330 additional ICE officers to coworking-style field offices across 40+ states, enabling larger and more frequent worksite operations than during the 2017-2019 period of Trump's first term.

title: Federal Judge Blocks Virginia's ICE Mask Ban Hours Before It Was Set to Take Effect
detail: U.S. District Judge Robert E. Payne issued a preliminary injunction on June 30, 2026 blocking Virginia's SB 352 and HB 1482 — which prohibited any law enforcement officer, including federal ICE agents, from wearing facial coverings while carrying out official duties in the Commonwealth and required visible name badges — hours before the law was set to take effect July 1. Governor Abigail Spanberger had signed SB 352 on May 20 alongside a separate executive order further restricting ICE activity in Virginia. Judge Payne found the Justice Department's lawsuit 'likely to succeed' on the merits that the law violated the intergovernmental immunity doctrine and Supremacy Clause by regulating how federal agents enforce federal immigration law, and cited evidence that unmasking could expose federal agents to 'real risk of physical harm.' The injunction remains in place pending resolution of the underlying DOJ suit, following a similar pattern to federal court rulings blocking California's SB 627 mask ban against federal agents earlier in 2026.
